claims.text: Liquid-phase pulsed laser ablation can synthesize equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Liquid-phase pulsed laser ablation ensures that these nanoparticles begin as a random solid solution.
Controlled low-temperature annealing enhances differential surface diffusion in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Differential atomic mobility selectively segregates lower-melting-point elements to the nanoparticle surface.
Annealing produces a low-melting-point-enriched surface layer that acts as a premelting nucleus.
A low-melting-point-enriched surface layer has lower local cohesive energy than a chemically homogeneous surface.
Lower surface cohesive energy facilitates surface disordering and causes premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
Rapid quenching preserves a chemically random elemental distribution in the nanoparticles.
Chemically homogeneous quenched nanoparticles have higher surface cohesive energy than annealed, surface-segregated nanoparticles.
Quenched nanoparticles have a higher surface-premelting onset temperature than annealed nanoparticles.
Annealed nanoparticles will form a detectable thin molten surface layer at a lower temperature than the quenched baseline.
The extent of lower-melting-point-element surface enrichment will correlate with the reduction in premelting-onset temperature.
Grain-size and oxidation-state analyses can establish that grain growth and oxidation are not responsible for the observed premelting change.
The proposed mechanism applies to CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles from 5 to 50 nm in size.
The proposed mechanism applies at heating rates from 0.5 to 10 degrees Celsius per minute.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-vacuum conditions during heating near the bulk melting point.
